name: libconfuse
reason: No numeric comparison anywhere reachable. README says only that it aims to be 'easy to use and quick to integrate'; no benchmark in README or docs, and a web search for parse-speed comparisons against inih, iniparser or libucl found none.

name: libelf
listed_description: Simple library for parsing ELF files.
reason: No numeric comparison. README (0intro/libelf, a small Plan 9 style reader with a readelfsection helper) has no performance text; a search for ELF parser benchmarks against elfutils libelf, LIEF or ELFIO found none naming it.

name: libfsm
listed_description: A library for building and executing finite state machines, including regex and glob.
reason: Directional claim only: README says supported patterns run in linear time and doc/advice.md says it avoids input-dependent slowdowns versus backtracking engines like PCRE, with no numbers. The reperf/boost.scr file is a benchmark script (Boost.Regex-style cases) with no results, and no shootout or paper with numbers was found.

name: libxls
listed_description: Read binary Excel files from C/C++
reason: No numeric comparison. README covers building and the xls2csv tool only; web searches for libxls timings against xlrd, calamine or Apache POI found none, and the ExcelBench suite does not include it.
